name: Sargent & Lundy, L.L.C.
headquarters: 77 W. Wacker Drive, Chicago, Illinois 60601 (moving from 55 E. Monroe Street; full occupancy planned by July 2027)
employees: '4,000 employees worldwide' (company, December 2024); 'over 4,000 people' (Engineering.com, April 2025); no newer first-party figure — the company says it 'nearly doubled its backlog and workforce' since 2023 and lists 'more than 1,500 openings worldwide' (January 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Sargent & Lundy is the 135-year-old Chicago architect-engineer that holds the owner's-engineer and independent-engineer seats on more of the power projects in this corpus than any firm except Burns & McDonnell and Black & Veatch, ranks first in nuclear and second in battery-storage design in ENR's 2026 Sourcebook, and has quietly built a data-centre practice — campus power, on-site generation, large-load interconnection and behind-the-meter nuclear — whose clients it names only as 'confidential hyperscaler' and 'confidential colocater'; it is privately owned by its own engineers, publishes no revenue, and is paid fees for judgment, never for equipment. BACKGROUND. Founded in 1891 by Frederick Sargent and Ayres Lundy; 'designed approximately 1,000 individual power plants during its history', 34 utility-scale new reactors, and currently serves 'over 90 operating nuclear units' in North America (company). Legal form Sargent & Lundy, L.L.C.; the company's own description is 'privately owned and led by engineers' — 'the people who own and manage our company – the dedicated engineers of Sargent & Lundy'. It does not use the words ESOP or employee-owned on any first-party channel, it does not appear on the NCEO Employee Ownership 100, and its CFO administers 'the firm's defined benefit plan'; the widely repeated 'employee-owned' label is third-party shorthand for an LLC held by its engineer-principals (collection gap: the ownership instrument is not disclosed). Twelve service lines from nuclear, grid, conventional power and renewables to data centres, decarbonisation, consulting and government services; 42 North American offices and five international including the L&T-Sargent & Lundy joint venture in Vadodara, India (since 1995). Two acquisitions in its history — ARES Corporation's Energy Services Division (2019) and Summit Engineering Services (2020). Three facts anchor the ecosystem read. First, the visible independent-engineer and owner's-engineer record: owner's engineer on Ørsted's Eleven Mile (300 MW solar plus 300 MW / 1,200 MWh BESS, Arizona), independent engineer on Leeward's Big Plain and Oak Trail solar financings and on Lotus Infrastructure's Ten West Link 500 kV line, technical adviser to EWEC on the UAE's first 400 MW / 800 MWh BESS tender, independent engineer for EVgo's DOE loan guarantee of up to USD 1.05 billion and for Macquarie's USD 2.4 billion Dow asset acquisition — 'nearly 25 gigawatts of solar, wind, battery storage, and other clean energy technologies' in owner's and independent engineering, 'over 7 GW' of storage experience. Second, nuclear: TVA's owner's engineer and detailed-design lead for the Clinch River BWRX-300 alongside Bechtel and GE Vernova Hitachi; NRC-inspected design packages for the Palisades restart and the Dow / X-energy Xe-100 site; the 2020 top-ten nuclear services clients read TVA, Exelon, Dominion, PSEG, AEP, DTE, Xcel Energy, Southern Nuclear, APS and Ameren. Third, data centres: a service page that offers 'Powered Shell Data Center Campus Design', 'On-Site Generation Projects', 'Grid Interconnection' and 'Owner's Engineering', a project sheet with two confidential hyperscalers and two confidential colocation operators, and a stated seat on the NERC Large Loads Task Force — none of it corroborated by any client or third party, which is the pattern for a fee-for-service engineer whose clients do the announcing. Collection gap, stated: no revenue, margin or backlog figure exists on any channel (Crain's and ENR revenue columns are paywalled; Forbes' 3,500-employee figure is stale); the ENR ranks are the only comparable series. The ownership instrument, the exact headcount after 2024, and every data-centre client name are undisclosed.
ecosystemRole: The second `advisor` in this corpus and the owner's-engineer counterpart to DNV's lender's-engineer profile: where DNV writes the report the bank relies on, Sargent & Lundy more often writes the specification the bidders answer, reviews the EPC's 30, 60 and 90 percent designs on the owner's behalf, witnesses the factory tests and oversees commissioning — and, when a lender needs it, sits as independent engineer too. It designs (engineer of record on Entergy Texas' 1,215 MW Orange County station; reactor-building standard plant for GE Hitachi's BWRX-300) and will take EPC scope only with a constructor partner (TIC, PCL, Boldt). In the AI data-centre chain it is the engineer between the hyperscaler and the utility: mock system-impact studies to pick a point of interconnection, large-load applications, substation design for 'hyperscaler digital campuses' in PJM, ERCOT, SPP and WECC, feasibility of islanded gas plants and of behind-the-meter nuclear. It is named by Entergy, TVA, Bechtel, GE Vernova, Mitsubishi Power and Duke; it competes with Burns & McDonnell, Black & Veatch, Kiewit Engineering, WSP (POWER Engineers), Stantec and DNV.

productsAndServices.name: Owner's engineering — generation, storage, transmission and data-centre campuses
productsAndServices.description: Representation of the asset owner from concept through commissioning: functional requirements and design basis, conceptual (10 and 30 percent) designs as a basis for contracting, EPC specification and bid review, 30/60/90 percent and issued-for-construction design reviews, procurement and vendor qualification, factory-acceptance-test witnessing, construction monitoring, commissioning and performance-test oversight, and O&M strategy.
highlights: Scope in the company's words: 'Following the award of an EPC contract, we perform engineering design reviews and construction oversight on the owner's behalf. We help evaluate whether EPC contractors have designed and constructed the facility in accordance with contract documents and industry standards' — with 'Conducting 30%, 60%, 90%, and issued for construction (IFC) engineering design package reviews', 'Monitoring on-site construction and owner's representative services' and 'Supporting commissioning and performance testing'.

Ørsted's Eleven Mile Solar Center, Pinal County, Arizona — 300 MW solar PV with an AC-coupled 300 MW / 1,200 MWh BESS, a stated USD 1 billion investment: 'Ørsted contracted Sargent & Lundy as owner's engineer', delivering 'BESS technical specification development and subsequent design reviews of the project's solar PV, BESS, substation, and generation interconnect-line designs' plus PPA and permitting reviews (start August 2022, COD October 2024).

Data-centre owner's engineering as the company describes it: 'We often begin work at project inception, defining functional requirements and developing a project design basis and equipment specifications … During procurement, we assess vendor qualifications, equipment specifications, and delivery timelines, helping owners avoid overdesign, scope gaps, or incompatible systems. We also monitor factory acceptance tests (FATs) and oversee critical commissioning procedures.' Named engagement: owner's engineer for 'a natural gas-fired islanded power and data center project to achieve 99.995% uptime' for a confidential colocation operator.

Scale claims: 'Currently, we support over 5 GW of solar PV projects in the role of owner's engineer'; 'The firm has provided owner's engineering and independent engineering for nearly 25 gigawatts of solar, wind, battery storage, and other clean energy technologies' (May 2026).

Nuclear owner's engineer: 'We have served as TVA's owner's engineer, and we are currently performing early site works in preparation for the construction permit application' at Clinch River, where TVA also has it 'lead the detailed design for the site-specific implementation of the BWRX-300' (World Nuclear News, 2025-01-24); owner's engineer to NRG for the proposed South Texas Project units 3 and 4 (2007) and to Cleco for the Diamond Vault carbon-capture project (2022).

Earthrise Energy's 270 MW Archtop solar project, Illinois: owner's engineer for a design that reuses an existing gas peaker's interconnection to skip the queue — 'the first of five solar power facilities' on 'more than 1.4 gigawatts' of existing grid connections (2025-10-20).
productsAndServices.positioning: The definitional contrast, in a third party's words: an EPC 'is responsible for delivering the project' under 'a lump-sum or turnkey contract with owner', whereas the owner's engineer 'independently represents the asset owner's interests' under 'a professional services agreement with owner' and bears no construction risk (Sarom Global, 2026). Burns & McDonnell (ENR's No. 1 power design firm for a decade) and Black & Veatch (No. 1 solar, No. 2 battery storage in 2025) are the direct competitors; Sargent & Lundy's edge is nuclear-grade quality systems ('extremely high-reliability backup power systems to the nuclear industry') applied to data-centre power.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Professional-services agreements with owners — hourly or lump-sum fees; the company describes itself as a 'full-service architect engineering firm' and reports to ENR's professional-services list, which ranks 'revenue from construction and program management fees'.
targetSegments: Nuclear plant owners and SMR developers
productsAndServices.roadmap: No product roadmap in the usual sense; the visible direction is the January 2025 appointment of a senior vice president 'responsible for the firm's nuclear power-related data center initiatives' and a 2026 Los Angeles office for 'large-scale substation and transmission line programs'.

productsAndServices.name: Independent engineering and due diligence for lenders, investors and buyers
productsAndServices.description: Technical due diligence supporting debt, tax equity, government loan guarantees and acquisitions: equipment and performance review, contract review, liquidated-damages terms, financial-model inputs, energy-yield assessment, construction monitoring with site visits and drawdown support, and operating-phase assessments for loan and reserve covenants.
highlights: The company's scope statement: 'We provide due diligence and independent engineering services for energy asset financings and investments, for lenders, investors, utilities, developers, asset owners, and prospective buyers. These services include equipment and performance reviews; commercial and technical contract reviews; environmental and permitting evaluations; liquidated damage terms reviews; financial model inputs evaluations; resource and energy yield assessments; and technical risk assessments.' And: 'Our independent and lender's engineering services include construction monitoring, with site visits conducted throughout the construction period.'

The BESS due-diligence method, from the firm's white paper: four review pillars — 'the planned use case(s) and revenue streams; equipment selections and the system design; commercial agreements; and construction, commissioning, and operating plans' — with the BESS-specific warning that 'Battery warranty terms are of concern because commercial protections are contingent on adherence to the BESS's operational limitations (depth of discharge, cycles, temperature, etc.)' and that 'The interdependence of the BESS use case, system design, and commercial terms necessitates an integrated full scope due diligence review be performed.'

Named mandates: independent engineer for Leeward Renewable Energy's Big Plain (196 MW, Ohio) and Oak Trail (100 MW, North Carolina) solar financings — 'Supported both debt lenders and tax equity investors. Visited each site monthly from mid-2022 through mid-2023'; independent engineer on Lotus Infrastructure's Ten West Link 500 kV, 125-mile Arizona–California line, including 'financial model assessment to support project financing'; independent engineer for EVgo's Department of Energy loan guarantee 'up to $1.05 billion' (2024); due diligence behind Macquarie Asset Management's USD 2.4 billion purchase of 40 percent of five Dow power and pipeline assets (2025); independent engineering review of Transition Equity Partners' USD 54 million investment in module maker Heliene (2024); technical viability assessment of a 30 MW / 36 MWh Merus Power / Alpiq BESS in Finland (2024).

Nuclear due diligence: 'We've gained relevant experience conducting due diligence reviews in support of asset acquisitions, U.S. Department of Energy financing, private equity investors, tax equity financing, and debt lenders … our team also reviews and stress tests financial models, revenue assumptions, and cost forecasts.'

The market's description of the seat: 'the independent engineer is typically selected by the lender but paid by the developer/owner' (Wikipedia); 'IEs serve as the gatekeepers of project bankability' and 'IEs identify issues. OEs help solve them' (EPE Consulting, 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: On lender panels alongside DNV, Black & Veatch, Burns & McDonnell, Leidos and UL Solutions. A 2026 overview assigns Sargent & Lundy the 'interconnection studies and engineering design' lane and DNV the bankability-report lane, but the firm's white papers and the Leeward, Ten West and EVgo mandates show it sells the full IE report. Its differentiator is the same engineering depth it uses as designer — an IE that has been engineer of record on 180 combustion-turbine projects reads an EPC design differently.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Fee-for-service mandates, lender-appointed and typically developer-paid per market practice; no equity, no guarantees.
targetSegments: Government lenders (DOE Loan Programs Office, EXIM)

productsAndServices.name: Energy storage engineering and utility technical advisory
productsAndServices.description: BESS design and engineering, use-case and specification development, interconnection and electrical studies, code and safety review, commissioning and testing-plan review, and procurement-side technical advisory to utilities buying storage under new contract forms.
highlights: 'With over 7 GW of experience spanning more than a decade, we are a recognized leader in the ESS industry' — 'both long- and short-duration ESS projects' across 'electrochemical, thermal, mechanical, gravity, and hydrogen' technologies (Grid page). Applications listed: 'Energy arbitrage. Frequency regulation. Black start. Power back-up. Solar and wind smoothing … Overload and congestion management. VAR support. Distribution, transmission, and substation cost deferral.'

Technical adviser to Emirates Water & Electricity Company on the UAE's first BESS IPP (400 MW, up to 800 MWh): 'supporting the development of the application and use case for the BESS and developing the technical specifications and performance requirements for the procurement package' and participating 'in the creation of a new energy storage agreement' (2024-08-14) — the buyer's-side counterpart to the IE's use-case test.

Owner's-engineer deliverables on Eleven Mile's 1,200 MWh battery: 'owner's engineer BESS technical specification development and subsequent design reviews … to assess engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) design deliverables for code compliance, prudent industry standards and best practices, operational safety considerations, performance, reliability, constructability', plus 'System design review of solar PV, co-located AC-coupled BESS, substation, and generation interconnect-line designs (e.g., fire protection, electrical, civil, and structural)' and 'Commissioning and testing plans review'.

Design capability: an 18 MW PJM frequency-response BESS in Pennsylvania with 'a new 115 kV substation … 115/34.9 kV generator step up transformer and a 34.5 kV feeder array to three 6 MW battery enclosures', 'Dynamic Modeling and Relay Coordination. OEM Interface and Coordination. Construction and Commissioning Management' (2015); a BART wayside-storage feasibility study valuing 2 MW units in the CAISO market.
ENR Sourcebook battery-storage design rank: No. 5 (2025) to No. 2 (2026) — 'its highest Battery Storage ranking to date'.

Collection gap: the firm names neither NFPA 855 nor UL 9540A anywhere on its channels; its formulation is that fire protection 'must be verified to be in accordance with local and national standards' and that its experts sit on NFPA committees.
productsAndServices.positioning: Black & Veatch (No. 2 in 2025) and Burns & McDonnell are the storage-design peers; DNV sells the independent-engineer and certification layer but does not design plants. The Sargent & Lundy pitch is the integration of use case, design and commercial terms in one review — the argument its own white paper makes.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owner's-engineer and technical-adviser contracts; design and EPCM scopes; two-day ESS training courses delivered at utility sites.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre power — campus design, on-site generation, large-load interconnection
productsAndServices.description: Powered-shell campus design (conceptual through 30 percent), medium-voltage and backup-generation sizing, siting and permitting, feasibility of on-site gas, nuclear and renewable generation, grid-prospecting and mock system-impact studies, large-load interconnection applications and utility negotiation, behind-the-meter and bridging-power design, and reliability, availability and maintainability (RAM) and techno-economic modelling.
highlights: The pitch, verbatim: 'We work with some of the largest energy consumers in the world to advise on and develop realistic and achievable power supply plans. We leverage our experience providing extremely high-reliability backup power systems to the nuclear industry to meet the challenges posed by high-consumption and mission-critical data center customers … We also supply full turnkey data center design.'

Interconnection method: 'We perform mock system impact studies to evaluate grid capacity and quantify expected network upgrade costs … Our system impact studies enable clients to submit load and interconnect requests at economically viable points of interconnection rather than waiting for opaque and costly study results'; 'we act as the client's technical advisor during engagement with the utility, managing milestone schedules, responding to technical queries, and negotiating interconnection agreements'; 'We also support compliance with evolving interconnection standards based on our participation in the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Large Loads Task Force (LLTF).'

Named-but-anonymous engagements (Data Center Projects sheet): owner's engineer for 'a natural gas-fired islanded power and data center project to achieve 99.995% uptime and mission critical reliability'; an 'off-grid power supply study' for simple- and combined-cycle gas turbines with integrated solar PV for 'a planned large data center campus'; for a 'Confidential Hyperscaler', the 'technical basis for carbon-free solutions to power data centers … existing utility-scale nuclear reactors, new advanced modular reactors (AMRs), and new small modular reactors (SMRs)' with 'A quantitative availability model' and 'A data center campus site plan'; 'ongoing due diligence activities for new data center campuses colocated adjacent to utility-scale power sources in all independent system operator regions'; substation design for 'hyperscaler and colocater digital campuses' for two confidential utilities; 'dozens of confidential power supply projects … in territories where PJM, ERCOT, SPP, and WECC provide service, delivering power to major data center developers'.

On-site generation: 'For islanded sites that are completely independent from the grid, we leverage our history of power generation experience to develop robust plans for scheduled maintenance and accommodate forced outage scenarios to achieve reliability goals'; RAM studies with 'Monte Carlo simulations' and 'mean time between failure (MTBF) and mean time to repair (MTTR)' against 'uptime guarantees and service level agreement (SLA) compliance'.

Behind-the-meter nuclear, from the Nuclear Power page: 'clients connect new electric loads to the station's generation output before a transmission service supplier meters the electricity … Potential industrial applications associated with BTM electricity include hydrogen generation, data centers, reverse osmosis, direct air capture, and artificial intelligence processing centers. We provide support for nearly all these applications.'

Collection gap: no client, regulator or trade-press source names Sargent & Lundy on any data-centre campus, behind-the-meter plant or large-load study; the only outside reference is a 2025 profile listing 'Data center power systems and AI infrastructure support' among its work. Every data-centre client is confidential by the company's choice.
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with Burns & McDonnell, Black & Veatch, Kiewit Engineering and the utilities' own planning groups for campus power, and with HDR, Jacobs and the specialist data-centre engineers for the building. Its distinct claim is nuclear-derived reliability engineering and the ability to design the generating plant, the substation and the interconnection as one scope; its distinct gap is that it can show no named data-centre client.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owner's-engineer, design and consulting contracts with hyperscalers, colocation operators, developers and utilities; exhibitor at Data Center World 2025 (Booth 144) and Data Center World Power 2025.

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear — new build, SMR licensing and design, restarts, uprates and life extension
productsAndServices.description: Architect-engineer and owner's-engineer services on new reactors and SMRs (standard-plant design, site-specific design, construction permit and combined licence applications, environmental reports, PSARs), restart engineering, power uprates, subsequent licence renewal, digital modernisation, and behind-the-meter industrial applications of operating plants.
highlights: Clinch River (TVA, BWRX-300): 'Sargent & Lundy will lead the detailed design for the site-specific implementation of the BWRX-300 at Clinch River, continuing a 40-year relationship with TVA' (World Nuclear News, 2025-01-24); DOE awarded the project USD 400 million under the Generation III+ SMR programme in December 2025; TVA's 2026 Valley Supplier Award followed (September 2026).

GE Hitachi: 'working directly with General Electric Hitachi (GEH) since 2023 … responsible for GEH's reactor building standard plant design' — an NRC vendor inspection in July 2025 sampled 'GEH's BWRX-300 control rod drive system mechanical design' among Sargent & Lundy's safety-related packages and found 'No findings of significance'.

Dow / X-energy Long Mott (Seadrift, Texas, four Xe-100 units, 320 MW): construction permit application filed under 10 CFR Part 50 in March 2025 with Sargent & Lundy providing 'site selection, licensing, and environmental services', the environmental report (with WSP) and the preliminary safety analysis report; the NRC issued its environmental assessment and finding of no significant impact in August 2026 — 'the first grid-scale advanced nuclear power plant built to serve an industrial site in the U.S.' (Shiven Sulkar).

Palisades restart (Holtec): the only restart the company names — a vice president is 'overseeing the firm's support for the restart of the once-decommissioned Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan' — and the NRC's 2025 inspection sampled its 'Auxiliary Feedwater Controllers replacement for Palisades' design package. Crane Clean Energy Center and Duane Arnold: no role found on any channel.

Fleet services: 'over 35 measurement uncertainty recapture (MUR) power uprates and more than 45 stretch and extended power uprates (SPUs/EPUs) since 2000'; 'over 300 large digital upgrades'; primary vendor for Entergy Arkansas' ANO-1 subsequent licence renewal (to 2054) and TVA's Browns Ferry SLR; the 2020 top-ten nuclear services clients were 'TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY, EXELON, DOMINION, PSEG, AEP, DETROIT EDISON, XCEL ENERGY, SOUTHERN NUCLEAR, ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY, AMEREN' (NRC pre-submittal slides, 2021).

ENR Sourcebook nuclear design rank No. 1 in 2026, 'a distinction the firm has earned eight times in the past decade'. NuScale strategic relationship and standard-plant design (2019–2022, 'over 11,000 design deliverables'); Curio's NuCycle fuel-recycling facility conceptual design (July 2026); Samsung Heavy Industries floating-SMR platform MoU (July 2026); US State Department FIRST/SPRING programme delivery in 14 countries.
productsAndServices.positioning: The incumbent architect-engineer for the US operating fleet ('the engineer of choice for nearly all operating U.S. nuclear power plants') and the design partner of choice for BWRX-300, Xe-100 and NuScale deployments; Bechtel builds, Kiewit and Fluor compete on construction and EPCM, Burns & McDonnell and Black & Veatch (Cascade JV) compete on SMR owner's engineering. For the data-centre chain the relevant asset is that this is the firm a hyperscaler hires to evaluate a reactor.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year engineer-of-choice and project-services agreements (Bruce Power's 'approximately $85 million per year' agreement is the only disclosed value), licensing and design contracts, government programme contracts.

productsAndServices.name: Grid — transmission, substations, interconnection studies and HVDC
productsAndServices.description: Overhead and underground transmission design to 765 kV, greenfield and brownfield substations from 13.8 to 765 kV including gas-insulated designs, SVC/STATCOM/HVDC/FACTS engineering, power-system studies (PSS/E, PSCAD, TARA, PSLF, ETAP), generator and large-load interconnection support across RTOs, NERC CIP assessments, and training courses.
highlights: 'reliable, safe, and cost-effective overhead transmission line designs, up to 765kV AC and HVDC'; substations 'in a multitude of configurations, 13.8kV – 765kV', with 'extensive experience in gas-insulated substations … static synchronous compensators (STATCOM), high voltage direct current (HVDC), and other flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS)'.

Studies: 'steady-state power flow and contingency analysis, reactive compensation studies, transient stability analysis, short circuit, harmonics, insulation coordination, subsynchronous resonance' for thermal, solar, storage, wind and hybrid interconnections — plus 'Large-load interconnection application support for data centers and other large loads'.

Named work: engineer of record on Lotus Infrastructure's Cielo Azul 500 kV switchyard in Arizona, which 'facilitates the interconnection of 2,700 megawatts of solar and battery energy storage system power'; independent engineer on Ten West Link (500 kV, 125 miles, '3,800 amps continuous with 25% series compensation'); BGE's Key Crossing Reliability Initiative with 397-foot monopoles 'the tallest in the Americas'; technical adviser to Samsung C&T / ADNOC on Project Lightning's subsea HVDC links (2 × 1 GW at ±320 kV) including a grid-code compliance report; NIPSCO 345 kV lines (EPC, 2017).

ENR Sourcebook transmission and distribution rank No. 8 (2026), 'top 10 … for the 10th consecutive year'; STATCOM tutorials 'for transmission systems and large-load applications such as data centers' at IEEE PES in 2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with Burns & McDonnell, Black & Veatch, WSP (which bought POWER Engineers for USD 1.78 billion in 2024), Stantec and HDR; the data-centre angle is that the same group that designs the hyperscaler's substation also runs the mock system-impact study that chose the site.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Design, EPC (with constructors) and study contracts with utilities, developers and transmission owners.
targetSegments: Renewable and storage developers in interconnection queues
Data-centre developers seeking points of interconnection

productsAndServices.name: Conventional generation — gas combined cycle, peakers and reciprocating engines
productsAndServices.description: Architect-engineer, engineer of record, owner's engineer and EPC (with constructor partners) on combustion-turbine plants, reciprocating-engine plants and repowering, including hydrogen-capable and hydrogen co-firing designs, with commissioning management.
highlights: 'We have provided engineering and design, owner's engineering, repowering, and related services for more than 180 combustion turbine projects around the world … totaled more than 37,000 megawatts (MW) of capacity'; 'In 1957, we designed the first utility combined cycle application in the U.S.'; reciprocating engines: 'approximately 500 megawatts (MW) of new capacity'.

Entergy Texas' Orange County Advanced Power Station, 1,215 MW, two Mitsubishi Power M501JAC turbines, hydrogen-capable, COD 2026: 'Sargent & Lundy, known for its advanced class combined-cycle engineering experience, is the Engineer of Record' in an EPC consortium with Mitsubishi Power and TIC as constructor (POWER, 2023-03-03) — 'the firm's first J-class combustion turbine design'.

Tampa Electric's South Tampa Resiliency Project at MacDill Air Force Base — 72 MW on four Wärtsilä 18V50SG engines, 'Designed with islanding capability … capable of forming a microgrid', an ENR Southeast Best Project award of merit in 2026; Lakeland Electric's 120 MW McIntosh plant on six MAN 18V51/60G engines 'able to burn up to 5% hydrogen'; Tampa Electric's 1,090 MW Big Bend modernisation on two GE 7HA.02 units.

Hydrogen: engineer of record on NYPA's Brentwood hydrogen-blending pilot with GE (2022) and partner on Duke Energy's DeBary power-to-power demonstration (2023); ENR fossil-fuel design rank No. 2 (2025), No. 3 (2026).

Relevance to data centres: the same simple- and combined-cycle and reciprocating-engine engineering is what the 'off-grid power supply study' for a large data-centre campus and the islanded 99.995 percent-uptime project draw on.
productsAndServices.positioning: Behind Burns & McDonnell and Black & Veatch on ENR's fossil-fuel design list but the only one of the three with a first J-class engineer-of-record credit in the 2020s; Kiewit and Zachry compete as EPCs with in-house engineering.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Engineer-of-record and owner's-engineer contracts; EPC only in consortium or joint venture with a constructor (TIC, PCL — White Oak Power Constructors; Boldt — Westside Energy Partners); EPCM.

recentDevelopments.headline: TVA presents Sargent & Lundy its 2026 Valley Supplier Award; the relationship 'began in February 1994' with 'no gap in service'
recentDevelopments.read: The owner's-engineer seat on the first US utility SMR is an extension of a 32-year account, not a competitive win.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRC issues its environmental assessment and finding of no significant impact for Long Mott Energy (Dow) and X-energy's four-unit Xe-100 plant at Seadrift; Sargent & Lundy prepared the environmental report with WSP and expects the PSAR review 'to be completed by year-end'
recentDevelopments.read: The first industrial-site advanced reactor to clear NRC's environmental gate did so on a Sargent & Lundy licensing package — the credential a hyperscaler evaluating nuclear will ask for.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sargent & Lundy discusses floating nuclear plants at the NEI/DOE industry day after signing a July MoU with Samsung Heavy Industries for a 'floating small modular reactor standard platform' designed to accept any reactor type
recentDevelopments.read: A platform play: standardise the plant around the reactor rather than the reactor itself, with the architect-engineer as the integrator.

recentDevelopments.headline: Grid-forming versus grid-following, black start and hybrid dispatch: Sargent & Lundy's storage consultant previews an Intersolar Middle East paper citing Eleven Mile, the UAE BESS, Archtop and the PJM frequency-response battery
recentDevelopments.read: The storage credential list the firm chooses to lead with — owner's engineering and use-case design, not cell testing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Curio engages Sargent & Lundy for siting, environmental, licensing and conceptual design of the NuCycle used-fuel recycling facility
recentDevelopments.read: Fuel-cycle facilities are the next licensing frontier and the firm is positioning as the architect-engineer for them.

recentDevelopments.headline: Named No. 89 on TIME's inaugural America's Best Private Companies list; the release restates that the firm 'remains privately owned and led by engineers'
recentDevelopments.read: The ownership formulation the firm uses every time — engineer-owned, not employee-owned — is deliberate and repeated.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR Sourcebook 2026: Sargent & Lundy No. 1 in nuclear plants, No. 2 in battery storage (from No. 5), No. 3 in fossil fuel, No. 8 in transmission and distribution
recentDevelopments.read: Three places gained in battery storage in one year is the clearest public signal of where the design book is growing.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR ranks the firm No. 26 among Top 50 construction managers and No. 56 in CM/PM-for-fee
recentDevelopments.read: Fee-based programme management is a growing line — the firm is selling supervision, not just drawings.

recentDevelopments.headline: US State Department SPRING initiative advances with Sargent & Lundy-led SMR licensing and financing workshops in Budapest, Dubrovnik and Tallinn across 14 countries
recentDevelopments.read: Government programme delivery gives the firm a standing role in how allied regulators frame SMR licensing.

recentDevelopments.headline: At PDOC a Sargent & Lundy transmission planner presents the 'technical, regulatory, and operational challenges planners and owners face when integrating large loads such as data centers into the transmission grid'
recentDevelopments.read: Large-load interconnection has become a named speaking topic three times in 2026 — the firm wants to be seen as the engineer of that queue.

recentDevelopments.headline: CLEANPOWER 2026: the firm cites 'owner's engineering and independent engineering for nearly 25 gigawatts of solar, wind, battery storage, and other clean energy technologies'
recentDevelopments.read: The first aggregate OE-plus-IE figure the firm has published — the size of its lender- and owner-side book in clean energy.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR Top 500 Design Firms: No. 22 overall, 'fourth consecutive year of upward movement'; No. 3 in power
recentDevelopments.read: Rank is the only comparable series a private engineer publishes; it has moved the right way every year since the 2023 CEO change.

recentDevelopments.headline: IEEE PES T&D in Chicago: Sargent & Lundy's planner joins a panel on 'Challenges for Large-Load Interconnection and Operation' with system operators and data-centre leaders; a colleague runs an all-day grid-forming session
recentDevelopments.read: The two technical themes of the data-centre grid problem — large loads and inverter-based resources — with the firm's people on both stages.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sargent & Lundy is the 'primary vendor' for Entergy Arkansas' Arkansas Nuclear One Unit 1 subsequent licence renewal, extending operation to 2054, with further Entergy work at Grand Gulf, Waterford 3 and River Bend
recentDevelopments.read: Fleet life-extension is the annuity beneath the new-build headlines — and Entergy is now a client in both gas and nuclear.

recentDevelopments.headline: Slovakia confirms SMR viability at four sites following a Sargent & Lundy-led technical study under the State Department's Project Phoenix
recentDevelopments.read: Coal-to-nuclear siting studies are a repeatable export product.

recentDevelopments.headline: HQ footprint at 77 W. Wacker expanded by 66,000 sq ft to nearly 448,000 sq ft; 300 Chicago roles added in a year, about 200 more planned, 'more than 1,500 openings worldwide'
recentDevelopments.read: Real estate is the growth disclosure of a company that publishes no revenue: 60 percent more space than the old headquarters.

recentDevelopments.headline: CEO Vic Suchodolski keynotes POWERGEN alongside NVIDIA's senior managing director of energy and Google Cloud's global power lead; a colleague presents on air permitting for new data-centre generation
recentDevelopments.read: Sharing a stage with the chip vendor and the hyperscaler is the closest the firm comes to naming a data-centre client.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2026 executive appointments: senior vice presidents Golub (nuclear digital and AI), Mohanty (CTO), Webb; vice presidents including Carusona (SMR development), Daou (financing due diligence) and Weller (new Los Angeles office for transmission programmes)
recentDevelopments.read: Promotions track the growth lines — nuclear digital, financing diligence, West Coast transmission.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE awards TVA USD 400 million under the Generation III+ SMR programme for Clinch River; the team is TVA, Sargent & Lundy, GE Vernova Hitachi and Bechtel
recentDevelopments.read: Federal money now sits behind the project the firm is detailed-design lead on.

recentDevelopments.headline: A vice president named to Nuclear News' 40 Under 40 is 'overseeing the firm's support for the restart of the once-decommissioned Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan'
recentDevelopments.read: The only public statement of a Palisades role — the owner is not named, but the NRC's 2025 inspection of the firm's Palisades design package corroborates it.

recentDevelopments.headline: CEO wins POWER's Executive Leadership Award; the citation records 'company-record annual revenue, nearly doubled its backlog and workforce' and market-share gains in 'conventional gas, nuclear, transmission and distribution, hydrogen, and battery energy storage'
recentDevelopments.read: The only quantitative growth statement in the record, and it is a doubling since 2023 with no base disclosed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Owner's engineer for Earthrise Energy's 270 MW Archtop solar project, which reuses an existing gas peaker's grid connection to bypass the interconnection queue — first of five sites on 'more than 1.4 gigawatts' of existing connections
recentDevelopments.read: Queue arbitrage as an engineering product: the interconnection is the asset and the owner's engineer designs around it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Data Center World Power 2025: Sargent & Lundy presents on air permits for on-site data-centre generation, noting hyperscalers and colocators 'increasingly opting for on-site power generation using natural gas or renewable energy'
recentDevelopments.read: Permitting the behind-the-fence gas plant is where the firm's environmental practice meets the data-centre practice.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR international rankings: No. 49 Top 150 Global Design Firms; the L&T-Sargent & Lundy JV cites 'nearly 10 gigawatts of conventional combustion turbine projects across the Middle East and Africa' and a second UAE office opens
recentDevelopments.read: The Middle East book — gas turbines, the UAE's first BESS — is where the firm's storage advisory is most visible.

recentDevelopments.headline: Dow and X-energy's construction permit application for the Xe-100 plant at Seadrift is filed with Sargent & Lundy's site-selection, licensing and environmental work behind it
recentDevelopments.read: An industrial off-taker's reactor, licensed on the firm's paper — the template for a data-centre-owned reactor if one is ever filed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Macquarie Asset Management acquires 40 percent of five Dow power and pipeline assets (USD 2.4 billion) on the strength of Sargent & Lundy due diligence covering 'operations and maintenance, plant performance, financial models, environmental permitting and compliance'
recentDevelopments.read: Buy-side technical due diligence on operating assets is the same IE skill sold to a different client.

recentDevelopments.headline: TVA selects Bechtel, Sargent & Lundy and GE Hitachi for the Clinch River BWRX-300; 'Sargent & Lundy will lead the detailed design for the site-specific implementation'
recentDevelopments.read: The first US utility SMR gets a three-firm integrated delivery team with the architect-engineer, not the constructor, leading design.

recentDevelopments.headline: Independent engineering review supports Transition Equity Partners' USD 54 million investment in module maker Heliene's Minnesota plant
recentDevelopments.read: IE work extends to manufacturing — the same site-visit, budget and construction-plan review applied to a factory.

recentDevelopments.headline: Independent engineer for EVgo's Department of Energy loan guarantee of 'up to $1.05 billion' for about 7,500 fast-charging stalls, 'from pre-construction to completion'
recentDevelopments.read: A government lender's IE mandate — the Loan Programs Office accepting the firm's report as the technical basis for a billion-dollar guarantee.

recentDevelopments.headline: Technical adviser to EWEC on the UAE's first BESS IPP (400 MW, up to 800 MWh): use-case development, technical specifications and performance requirements, and 'a new energy storage agreement'
recentDevelopments.read: The buyer's engineer writing the specification that the bidders' IEs will later test — the other side of the same table.

periods.commentary: A private LLC with no filing obligation and no public debt. There is no consensus, no guidance and no rating — every 'expected' field is empty by design. The ENR rank is the closest thing to an audited series: it is compiled by a third party from self-reported revenue, so relative position is comparable even though the underlying numbers are not public. Read the 'nearly doubled' claim with its base in mind: 2023 was the first year of the current CEO.

financials.commentary: Sargent & Lundy publishes no income statement, balance sheet, backlog or margin, and no independent source has one: Crain's private-company list and ENR's revenue tables are paywalled and the firm's row could not be read. What can be said is directional and corroborated — record revenue and a doubled backlog and workforce since 2023 (company), a rising ENR rank each year since (ENR), a headquarters 60 percent larger than the one it left (company), and 'more than 1,500 openings' (company). The ownership instrument is undisclosed: the firm says 'privately owned and led by engineers'; it is not an NCEO-listed ESOP and its CFO administers a defined-benefit plan. The one equity position ever disclosed is an investment in NuScale Power (2019, amount undisclosed). No credit rating exists.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess Sargent & Lundy's commercial model is fee-for-judgment — architect-engineer, owner's engineer, independent engineer — and that it takes EPC exposure only with a constructor carrying the construction risk. Basis: every EPC credit in the record is a consortium or joint venture (TIC on Orange County, PCL in White Oak Power Constructors, Boldt in Westside Energy Partners, EC Source in ECSL for AEP, Kiewit on San Juan); the firm reports to ENR's fee-based professional-services list; its ESOP-free 'owned and led by engineers' structure has no external capital to put at risk. The one disclosed equity position (NuScale, 2019) is the exception that shows the rule.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess the firm's data-centre practice is real, growing and deliberately unnamed, and that the anonymity is the client's choice rather than a sign of thin work. Basis: a dedicated service page with six sub-services, a project sheet listing two confidential hyperscalers and two confidential colocation operators plus utility substation work for 'hyperscaler digital campuses' in four ISO regions, a 2025 senior-vice-president appointment for 'nuclear power-related data center initiatives', a NERC Large Loads Task Force seat, and speaking slots beside NVIDIA and Google Cloud — against zero third-party corroboration of any client. Fee-for-service engineers do not announce; owners do, and hyperscalers do not.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that nuclear is the firm's decisive differentiator in the AI-power market, because a hyperscaler weighing a reactor needs the one engineer that has licensed, designed and inspected them for seventy years. Basis: owner's engineer and detailed-design lead on Clinch River; standard-plant designer for GE Hitachi's BWRX-300 and NuScale; licensing author for Dow/X-energy's construction permit, now past NRC's environmental gate; the 'Confidential Hyperscaler' engagement on 'existing utility-scale nuclear reactors, new advanced modular reactors (AMRs), and new small modular reactors (SMRs)' with an availability model and a campus site plan; and a behind-the-meter nuclear page that names 'data centers' and 'artificial intelligence processing centers' as applications. Against: no restart other than Palisades is confirmed, and Constellation's Crane project names no engineer.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the storage practice has shifted from designer to buyer's and lender's engineer, and that this is the right side of the table for the next five years. Basis: the ENR battery-storage design rank rose from No. 5 to No. 2 while the named storage mandates are advisory — EWEC's tender specification, Eleven Mile's owner's engineering, the Finland due diligence, tax-equity IE work the firm calls 'one of the few tax-equity accepted independent engineers for BESS projects'. As storage financings move to merchant and hybrid structures the use-case-versus-warranty test in the firm's own white paper becomes the gating review, and the firm is on the panel.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the interconnection queue is the firm's most valuable consulting product, because it sells time. Basis: mock system-impact studies to choose a point of interconnection 'rather than waiting for opaque and costly study results'; FERC Order 845 'equal or better' conversions of wind to solar positions; the Archtop project's reuse of a peaker's connection 'to fast-track the grid interconnection process'; a white paper on converting renewable queue positions to thermal plants — 'growing demand for baseload power generation creates an opportunity to adapt planned solar and wind project developments for new thermal power facilities'. Each is a way to reach energisation years earlier, which is the scarce input in the data-centre chain.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the 'employee-owned' label attached to the firm by third parties overstates what is disclosed. Basis: the firm never uses the term, is absent from the NCEO Employee Ownership 100, describes itself as 'privately owned and led by engineers' with 'engineer owners', and its CFO administers a defined-benefit plan rather than an ESOP — consistent with an LLC held by its principals. The distinction matters for succession and for how a buyer would ever approach it; the instrument itself is a collection gap.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess the firm's public silence on the standards that govern its work — NFPA 855 and UL 9540A in storage, IEEE 2800 and PRC-029 in inverter compliance, NRC Part 53, ERCOT Senate Bill 6 — reflects a house style of describing capability rather than citing rules, not a gap in the capability. Basis: its people chair IEEE nuclear standards working groups, sit on NFPA committees and the NERC task force, and its BESS white paper says fire protection 'must be verified to be in accordance with local and national standards' without naming them. A reader should not infer inexperience from the absence of acronyms — but should ask.

Collection gap: no revenue, backlog, margin or headcount after 2024 exists on any channel; the ownership instrument is undisclosed; every data-centre client is confidential; the Palisades role is corroborated only by an NRC inspection sample and one profile; and white-paper PDFs are form-gated so only abstracts were read. The firm's own site was read in full (640 pages); third-party discovery was budget-limited.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *2026–2027 — a named data-centre client:* any hyperscaler, colocation operator or utility release naming Sargent & Lundy on campus power, on-site generation or a large-load study would convert Judgment 2 from inference to record. *By year-end 2026 — Long Mott PSAR review complete:* the firm expects it; completion keeps the Dow/X-energy permit on schedule and strengthens Judgment 3. *2027 — Clinch River construction permit application filed:* the firm is 'performing early site works in preparation'; filing would be the first US utility SMR permit application on its paper. *April 2027 — ENR Top 500 and July 2027 Sourcebook:* a fifth consecutive rise, and whether battery storage holds No. 2, is the only quantitative check on the growth claims. *July 2027 — full occupancy of 77 W. Wacker:* the physical test of the hiring claims. *Ecosystem check:* whether Sargent & Lundy or DNV appears as IE on the next US BESS financing that a covered developer announces.
